items.followUp: Define average speed and write its formula.

rubric.why: Checks the defining relationship for velocity.
rubric.description: Defines velocity as the rate of change of displacement with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this relationship clearly; accept equivalent wording such as displacement per unit time.
Award 1 mark for a correct formula using displacement divided by time.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.

items.followUp: Convert 72 km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Checks the correct conversion method and substitution.
rubric.description: Uses the conversion factor from km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹ and substitutes 50.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct conversion setup, such as multiplying by 5/18 or by 1000/3600.

rubric.description: Gives the speed in m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 13.89 m s⁻¹ (accept 13.9 m s⁻¹ or a correctly rounded equivalent).

modelAnswer: Formula: v in m s⁻¹ = v in km h⁻¹ × 5/18.

items.followUp: Define speed and state how it differs from velocity.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of rest in relation to a reference.
rubric.description: Defines rest as no change in position with time relative to the surroundings or a reference point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that position remains unchanged with time relative to the surroundings or reference point.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of motion in relation to a reference.
rubric.description: Defines motion as a change in position with time relative to the surroundings or a reference point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that position changes with time relative to the surroundings or reference point.

modelAnswer: A body is at rest if its position does not change with time relative to its surroundings.
A body is in motion if its position changes with time relative to its surroundings.

items.followUp: State one difference between static friction and sliding friction.

rubric.why: Checks the stated comparison between the two kinds of friction.
rubric.description: States that rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that rolling friction is less than sliding friction.

rubric.why: Checks the physical reason for the comparison.
rubric.description: Explains that rolling reduces the interlocking/contact or deformation effects responsible for sliding friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation involving less interlocking of surface irregularities, less contact, or reduced deformation during rolling.

modelAnswer: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.
During rolling, the surfaces do not slide over one another as much, so their irregularities interlock less and the friction is reduced.

items.followUp: Define centripetal force and write its formula.

rubric.why: Checks the nature and direction of centripetal acceleration.
rubric.description: Defines it as the acceleration of an object moving in a circular path, directed towards the centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying circular motion and the inward direction towards the centre.
Award 1 mark for a correct expression, a_c = v²/r.

modelAnswer: Centripetal acceleration is the acceleration of an object moving in a circular path, directed towards the centre of the circle.

items.followUp: Define the moment arm and state its SI unit.

rubric.description: Defines torque as the turning or rotational effect of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying torque as the turning effect of a force.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical relationship for torque.
rubric.description: Writes torque as force multiplied by the perpendicular distance (moment arm).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation using force and perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

items.followUp: What is the centre of mass of a body?

rubric.why: Checks the defining point and the action of the body's weight.
rubric.description: Identifies the centre of gravity as the point through which the whole weight of a body acts.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; award 1 mark if the response identifies the point but does not state that the whole weight acts through it.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which the whole weight of the body appears to act.

items.followUp: Define work and write its formula.

rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that power is work done per unit time.
Award 1 mark for a correct formula, P = W/t.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
P = work done / time taken = W/t.
